techniques.related_microoptimization: For arithmetic norm row-round q(t)=a+b*t+c*t^2, accumulate a and c only and recover b=claim-2*a-c; current code explicitly accumulates x*d. Handle equality-factor instance rounds separately.

techniques.projective_candidate: Use projective interpolation so a fold has form a+r*b. This changes the polynomial interpretation and requires adapting structured coefficient evaluation and BitZ terminal openings.
techniques.univariate_candidate: Existing test-only inner skip replaces several ordinary rounds with one higher-degree prefix. Its final Lagrange-weighted claims need two bridges to the original multilinear openings.
techniques.not_applicable_directly: The monomial paper's narrow upper-limb challenge optimization targets about256-bit fields; current126-bit field has no spare128-bit challenge domain to exploit that way.
techniques.security: New domains, round identities, terminal obligations and any degree/challenge changes require complete128-bit accounting and protocol versioning
failure_modes: Projective interpolation is different from the infinity extrapolation point already used by ordinary sumcheck
Bridge costs can erase univariate-skip gains
Reducing challenge entropy to cheap64-bit values would change the security budget
techniques.validation: Prototype full verifier and opening composition before claiming an end-to-end speedup
